---
title: "Glossary"
---

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Branch** | A separate line of development. `main` is the default branch. |
| **Clone** | A full copy of a repo, including its history, on your computer. |
| **Commit** | A saved snapshot of changes, with a message, an author, and a unique ID (hash). |
| **Commit message** | A short description of what a commit changed and why. |
| **Conflict (merge conflict)** | When two changes affect the same lines and Git needs you to choose which to keep. |
| **Diff** | The line-by-line difference between two versions of a file. |
| **Fetch** | Check GitHub for new changes without applying them. |
| **Fork** | Your own copy of someone else's repo on GitHub. |
| **.gitignore** | A file listing patterns for files Git should never track. |
| **GitHub Pages** | A free GitHub service that turns a repo into a website. |
| **HEAD** | The commit you are currently on. |
| **Issue** | A GitHub item for tracking a task, bug, or idea. |
| **Local** | Your computer's copy of a repo. |
| **main** | The default, official branch of a repo. |
| **Markdown (.md)** | A simple text formatting language used for READMEs and documentation. |
| **Merge** | Combine the changes from one branch into another. |
| **Organization (org)** | A shared GitHub account for a team, such as `nv-ose`. |
| **origin** | The default name for the remote copy of the repo on GitHub. |
| **Owner** | An org member with full admin rights. |
| **Pull** | Fetch new changes from GitHub and merge them into your local copy. |
| **Pull request (PR)** | A request to merge one branch into another, with review and discussion. |
| **Push** | Upload your local commits to GitHub. |
| **Push protection** | A GitHub feature that blocks pushes containing known secret formats. |
| **README** | The front-page document of a repo, usually `README.md`. |
| **Remote** | A copy of the repo hosted elsewhere, usually on GitHub. |
| **Repository (repo)** | A project folder tracked by Git, plus its history. |
| **Revert** | A new commit that undoes an earlier commit. |
| **Secret** | Any credential: a password, API key, token, or private key. |
| **Stage (staging area)** | The set of changes chosen to go into the next commit (`git add`). |
| **Template repository** | A repo you can use to start new repos with the same files, without its history. |
| **Two-factor authentication (2FA)** | A second login step, such as an app code, that protects your account. |
